recommendation: Keep the no-change audit commit. If DeviceUsage is later repatriated from the OO incubator into core, handle any context-versus-encounter rename as a separate current-version work-group decision.
issue_request: FHIR-17662 asked all applicable OO event and request resources to change .context back to .encounter, with cardinality 0..1 Reference(Encounter), and to make the event/workflow episode-of-care extension usable at the resource level.
initial_application: The Jira comment cites commit 7ea8dbba47af731f137a84550120bf1963408ca3, which applied GF#17662 to DiagnosticReport, Media, NutritionOrder, ServiceRequest, examples, and compartments. Earlier GF#17662 commits efd2a28750 and e6887f2aa8 handled DeviceRequest, and 886a9c0976 handled Task as a parallel OO resource.
additional_context: FHIR-17661 is the linked Observation-specific precedent for separating Encounter from EpisodeOfCare. In current core, DeviceRequest, DiagnosticReport, NutritionOrder, and ServiceRequest are active and already use .encounter; Media is retired; DeviceUseStatement is only a rename to DeviceUsage; and current module/resource-guide pages link DeviceUsage to the OO incubator IG rather than an active core resource. The former eventEpisodeOfCare extension is now maintained in the FHIR Extension Pack as workflow-episodeOfCare and includes contexts/search bases for the relevant resource family.
reconciliation: No source files were changed. The active current core resources in scope already define .encounter as 0..1 Reference(Encounter), and the only remaining old-style local DeviceUsage.context definition is outside active core build scope for this reconciliation.

related_jiras.note: Observation-specific context-to-encounter issue explicitly referenced by FHIR-17662.
Later Applied DeviceUseStatement/DeviceUsage workflow-mapping issue that maps DeviceUsage.context to Event.encounter but does not make DeviceUsage active in core.

evidence_items.summary: Published/Persuasive STU3 OO change request to rename applicable .context elements back to .encounter and allow the episode-of-care extension at resource level.
evidence_items.learned: This establishes final WG intent for the seed reconciliation.

evidence_items.summary: GF#17662 commits applied the context-to-encounter changes to historical OO spreadsheets/examples including DiagnosticReport, Media, NutritionOrder, ServiceRequest, DeviceRequest, and Task.
evidence_items.learned: The seed was previously implemented rather than left unapplied.

evidence_items.summary: Current active core definitions use DeviceRequest.encounter, DiagnosticReport.encounter, NutritionOrder.encounter, and ServiceRequest.encounter with max 1 and Encounter target profiles.
evidence_items.learned: The active current core source already matches the requested element name and type.

evidence_items.summary: fhir.ini lists the in-scope current resources and renames/retirements; current module pages link DeviceUsage to the OO incubator IG.
evidence_items.learned: DeviceUsage.context is not an active core build-scope defect for this seed, while Media is retired from core.

evidence_items.summary: The workflow-episodeOfCare extension and search parameter in the FHIR Extension Pack include contexts/bases for DeviceRequest, DeviceUsage/DeviceUseStatement, DiagnosticReport, NutritionOrder, and ServiceRequest.
evidence_items.learned: The extension-related part of the old issue is now maintained outside core and is present for the relevant family.

evidence_items.summary: 2018 committers discussion says FHIR-17662 was for resources outside Observation and was partially applied before Eric Haas completed it.
evidence_items.learned: This supports interpreting FHIR-17662 as the non-Observation companion to FHIR-17661 and confirms no contrary community conclusion was found.

evidence_items.summary: No existing reconcile commit was present, and current searches found encounter on active in-scope resources with only out-of-scope DeviceUsage retaining context.
evidence_items.learned: A single empty no-change audit commit is the correct non-duplicative publication.
